sourceName: EGBO IGI IWOSAN TI ILE YORUBA 2
title: OGUN HYPERTENSIN (EJE RIRU)
subtitle: (HIGH BLOOD PRESSURE)
preview: HIGH BLOOD PRESSURE · EGBO IGI IWOSAN TI ILE YORUBA 2
contentPreview: Page 2 • High Blood Pressure • Yoruba / English
contentYoruba:
(AO WA ODODO ORI AKO IGI IBEPE AO DA SINU OMIN TIWAN
BAFISE IRU AO FI SIBE FUN 4DAYS AFTER 4DAYS AO MA MU NIN
ARO ATI ALE NIGBATI AOBAFIMUN FUN OJO MEJE PELU ASE
OLORUN YIOTI KURO NIBE
contentEnglish: Obtain flowers from the top of a male pawpaw tree. Put them into the liquid described in the source as the water used for preparing iru, and add iru. Leave the mixture for four days. After the fourth day, take it in the morning and at night for seven days. The source says, with God’s grace, the high blood pressure will go away.

sourceName: EGBO IGI IWOSAN TI ILE YORUBA 2
title: OOGUN OGBE INU (ULCER)
subtitle: (STOMACH ULCER)
preview: STOMACH ULCER · EGBO IGI IWOSAN TI ILE YORUBA 2
contentPreview: Page 2 • Stomach Ulcer • Yoruba / English
contentYoruba:
Ao wa efo gbure ..ao gbo daada ti yio MUN bi igbati won ja
ewedu..ao gbe sori ina..ao ni fi omi sio..
Ao da gari si ti obati gbona daada..ao fi teba...ao wafi eba naa je obe
toba wuwa...walahi walahi walahi DANWO...kosi bi ulcer naa se pe
Lara to..
contentEnglish: Get efo gbure and cook it very well until it becomes thick and slippery like ewedu. Keep it on the fire as described in the source, then add garri when it is very hot and make eba from it. Eat the eba with any soup of your choice. The source presents this as a remedy for ulcer.

sourceName: EGBO IGI IWOSAN TI ILE YORUBA 2
title: OGUN NANRUN INUN ARA
subtitle: (BODY RASH / SKIN IRRITATION)
preview: BODY RASH / SKIN IRRITATION · EGBO IGI IWOSAN TI ILE YORUBA 2
contentPreview: Page 2 • Body Rash / Skin Irritation • Yoruba / English
contentYoruba:
(AO WA EWE APASA TIWANHUNPE NIN EWE IMIN ESU AOJA EWE
NAN AO DA SINU OMIN AO SE BI ENIN SE EFO AO WA LO ATA SI
AOFIRO EFO NAN PELU IRU AO FI EFO NAN JE EKO AO WA JA ESO ORI
IMIN ESU NAN AO WA SA TI YIOGBE AO WA GUN PAPO AO WA
DASINUN EPO OGERE AOMAFI RA OJU KOKORO TIOBA SUJADE
LARA WA PELU AGBARA OLORUN GBOGBO NANRU TIOBAWA
NINUN EJE GBOGBO RE NIN YIOKU
contentEnglish: Get ewe apasa, which the source also calls ewe imin esu. Prepare the leaves in water as one would prepare a vegetable soup, add pepper and iru, and eat the vegetable with eko. The source then instructs taking the fruit from the top of the imin-esu plant, drying it, pounding it, and mixing it into epo ogere. Apply the mixture to any skin eruptions that appear on the body. The source claims that, with God’s power, the irritation in the blood and on the skin will clear.

sourceName: EGBO IGI IWOSAN TI ILE YORUBA 2
title: ALASE FUN OBINRIN
subtitle: (WOMEN’S TRADITIONAL PREPARATION)
preview: WOMEN’S TRADITIONAL PREPARATION · EGBO IGI IWOSAN TI ILE YORUBA 2
contentPreview: Page 2 • Women’s Traditional Preparation • Yoruba / English
contentYoruba:
EEPO OSAN WEWE,OROGBO GBIGBE MERIN,ODIDI ATARE
KAN,ALO KANHUN,EGBO INABIRI,AO JO PAPO DADA, OBINRIN NAA
YIO MA FI EKO GBIGBONA LO.
contentEnglish: Materials named in the source: lime peel, four dried bitter kola, one whole atare, alo/kanhun, and inabiri root. Burn the materials together thoroughly. The woman is instructed to use a small amount with hot pap.

sourceName: EGBO IGI IWOSAN TI ILE YORUBA 2
title: ABIWERE
subtitle: (ABIWERE TRADITIONAL PREPARATION)
preview: ABIWERE TRADITIONAL PREPARATION · EGBO IGI IWOSAN TI ILE YORUBA 2
contentPreview: Page 2 • Abiwere Traditional Preparation • Yoruba / English
contentYoruba:
EWE ODUNDUN,AO LO YIO KUNNA DADA,AO FI ORI PO PAPO
DADA,OBINRIN NAA,YIO MA FI WO IKUN RE WA SI ISALE ODAJU.
contentEnglish: Grind ewe odundun very thoroughly and mix it well with ori (shea butter). The woman is instructed to rub the preparation downward over the abdomen. The source presents it as an Abiwere preparation.

sourceName: EGBO IGI IWOSAN TI ILE YORUBA 2
title: ROPAROSE / STROKE
subtitle: (STROKE)
preview: STROKE · EGBO IGI IWOSAN TI ILE YORUBA 2
contentPreview: Page 3 • Stroke • Yoruba / English
contentYoruba:
ALUBOSA AYU,AO GE SINU IGO,AO WA FI OMI IGBIN SI,AO MA MU

LOJOJUMO,OLOHUN KONI FI STROKE BA WA JA OO.
contentEnglish: Cut garlic/onion into a bottle and add snail water. The source gives two spoonfuls daily for an adult and one spoonful daily for a child, and presents the preparation as a traditional stroke remedy.

sourceName: EGBO IGI IWOSAN TI ILE YORUBA 2
title: FUN INU RIRUN

preview: ABDOMINAL PAIN / INTERNAL DISCOMFORT · EGBO IGI IWOSAN TI ILE YORUBA 2

contentEnglish: Put akogun into a bottle and soak it in cold water to make an infusion. The source instructs taking one spoonful daily for abdominal or internal discomfort.

sourceName: EGBO IGI IWOSAN TI ILE YORUBA 2
title: JEDIJEDI
subtitle: (JEDIJEDI / TRADITIONAL DIGESTIVE COMPLAINT)
preview: JEDIJEDI / TRADITIONAL DIGESTIVE COMPLAINT · EGBO IGI IWOSAN TI ILE YORUBA 2

EWE EFINRIN,EWE OWU AKESE,EWE EWURO,AO WA OMI TUTU

contentEnglish: Materials named in the source: ewe efinrin, ewe owu akese, ewe ewuro, cold water and a little salt. Prepare the leaves with the cold water and salt. The source instructs taking the preparation in the morning and at night for jedijedi.

sourceName: EGBO IGI IWOSAN TI ILE YORUBA 2
title: IDI YIYO
subtitle: (RECTAL / ANAL COMPLAINT)
preview: RECTAL / ANAL COMPLAINT · EGBO IGI IWOSAN TI ILE YORUBA 2
contentPreview: Page 3 • Rectal / Anal Complaint • Yoruba / English
contentYoruba:
AO FA PAKI EGE(CASSAVA) OLOMO KAN TU,AKO NI JE KI O KAN
MOLE,AO WA JO PAKI NAA PELU IYEPE ARARE ATI ODIDI ATARE
KAN,AO MA FI FOKO
contentEnglish: Peel the outer bark/skin from one cassava stem or piece as described in the source, keeping it from touching the ground. Burn the peel together with its own soil and one whole atare. The source says the resulting preparation is used with cold pap for the condition called idi yiyo.

sourceName: EGBO IGI IWOSAN TI ILE YORUBA 2
title: OGUN IKO
subtitle: (COUGH)
preview: COUGH · EGBO IGI IWOSAN TI ILE YORUBA 2
contentPreview: Page 3 • Cough • Yoruba / English
contentYoruba:
EGBO IPETE,EGBO IFON,AO GE KEKEKE SINU IKE RAGOLISI,AO BU
IYO DIE SI,AO WA TU OMI ORORO MAALUSI,AO WA GBE PAMO FUN
OJO META,AO MA MU NI SIBI KANKAN.
contentEnglish: Cut ipete root and ifon root into small pieces and place them in a Ragolis-type container. Add a little salt and pour in cow oil/fat as written in the source. Keep it for three days. The source instructs taking one spoonful at a time for cough.

sourceName: EGBO IGI IWOSAN TI ILE YORUBA 2
title: OGUN IKO IFE/AWUGBE (ASHTMA OR TB)
subtitle: (TUBERCULOSIS / PERSISTENT COUGH)
preview: TUBERCULOSIS / PERSISTENT COUGH · EGBO IGI IWOSAN TI ILE YORUBA 2
contentPreview: Page 3 • Tuberculosis / Persistent Cough • Yoruba / English
contentYoruba:
EWU OGAN, OBU OTOYO ADIN DUDU.
AO DA EWU OGAN YI SINU IKOKO ORU TI A O SUN TI YOO DI ERU, TI
O BA TI FE DUDU TAN AO FI OBU OTO YO SI NI IWON BA, AO JE KI
EWU OGAN TI ATI JO YEN KI O TUTU, A O WA BU ADIN SI, ENI NA
YOO MA MU NI SIBI KANKAN NI ARAARO.
contentEnglish: Materials named in the source: ewu ogan, obu otoyo and black palm-kernel oil. Burn the ewu ogan in a clay pot until it becomes ash. Add obu otoyo in the quantity described in the source, allow the burnt material to cool, then add black palm-kernel oil. The source instructs the person to take one spoonful in the morning and presents it for persistent cough, asthma or tuberculosis.

sourceName: EGBO IGI IWOSAN TI ILE YORUBA 2
title: ITUSILE YARA
subtitle: (PREMATURE EJACULATION)
preview: PREMATURE EJACULATION · EGBO IGI IWOSAN TI ILE YORUBA 2
contentPreview: Page 4 • Premature Ejaculation • Yoruba / English
contentYoruba:
Orogbo, obi gbanja,etu ibon,ako okuta,esuru funfun,ege tia fi ngun
iyan,ogede agbagba dudu,agbado ,iyere,ao fi sugar die si, ao gun
po,ao ma fi fo eko tutu mu.
contentEnglish: Materials named in the source: bitter kola, obi gbanja, gunpowder, ako okuta, esuru funfun, a piece of the yam-pounding pestle, ripe dark plantain, maize, iyere and a little sugar. Pound the materials together. The source instructs using the preparation with cold pap for quick ejaculation.

sourceName: EGBO IGI IWOSAN TI ILE YORUBA 2
title: AGBO INU IGO FUN ALE OKUNRIN* (MAN POWER)
titleOriginal: AGBO INU IGO FUN ALE OKUNRIN* (MAN POWER)
subtitle: (MALE SEXUAL VITALITY)
preview: MALE SEXUAL VITALITY · EGBO IGI IWOSAN TI ILE YORUBA 2
contentPreview: Page 4 • Male Sexual Vitality • Yoruba / English
contentYoruba:
Itaku gbonyingbonyin,Itaku eruju,ao ge mejeji sinu igo kan, ao wa
ro 7up si tabi oti oyinbo, gaasi kokan ni ojojumu.
2.Itaku gbonyingbonyin, Itaku Igongon,Itaku Aka,Itaku
idiapata,Itaku osun,Itaku ogbolo,Egbo Asunrun oyinbo,Egbo
Asunrun yoruba, Ako okuta were funfun mesan,Eso Abere
mewa,Iyere die,Konnofuru die. Ao ko okuta wewe pelu awon nkan
toku yen papo sinu igo, ao da oti oyinbo si, ao ma mu diedie. Odaju.
Omode lo nse mi ooo.
contentEnglish:
First version: cut itaku gbonyingbonyin and itaku eruju into a bottle, add 7UP or foreign liquor, and take one small measure daily.

Second version: the source lists itaku gbonyingbonyin, itaku igongon, itaku aka, itaku idiapata, itaku osun, itaku ogbolo, asunrun oyinbo root, asunrun Yoruba root, nine white ako-okuta-were stones, ten abere fruits, a little iyere and cloves. Put the small stones and the other materials into a bottle, add foreign liquor and take a small amount at a time. The source presents both versions as male-vitality preparations.

sourceName: EGBO IGI IWOSAN TI ILE YORUBA 2
title: OGUN IGBEBI FUN OBINRIN TO DE ORI IKUNLE
titleOriginal: OGUN IGBEBI FUN OBINRIN TO DE ORI IKUNLE
subtitle: (LABOUR / CHILDBIRTH SUPPORT)
preview: LABOUR / CHILDBIRTH SUPPORT · EGBO IGI IWOSAN TI ILE YORUBA 2
contentPreview: Page 4 • Labour / Childbirth Support • Yoruba / English
contentYoruba:
Ojo ti agbami ojo ba ro, ao lo si ona oko tabi odo, ao mu igo ofifo tabi
ado ato lowo, ao ri awon ekolo dudu kan, awon miran npe ni kola
tabi olooji, o ni pon to ika, o we lorun bi okoto, ao fi owo lale siwaju
ekolo na, ao fi igo tabi ato yen niwaju re, ao je ko bo sile fun rare, ao
ko opolopo atare le lori, to ba di ehin ojo keje ti obinrin na ba de ori
ikunle ao fun ni mesan tabi mewa ninu atare na, wipe kio je pelu
omi gbona idaji tombila.
contentEnglish: On a day of heavy rain, the source instructs going toward a farm road or river with an empty bottle or container. It describes finding a dark insect/worm called kola or olooji, placing the container in front of it and allowing it to enter by itself, then placing many atare seeds on it. On the seventh day, when the woman reaches labour, the source instructs giving her nine or ten of the atare seeds with about half a tumbler of hot water. This is presented as a traditional childbirth preparation.

sourceName: EGBO IGI IWOSAN TI ILE YORUBA 2
title: OGUN ALASE TI OBINRIN KO BARI NKAN OSU RE
titleOriginal: OGUN ALASE TI OBINRIN KO BARI NKAN OSU RE
subtitle: (MENSTRUAL COMPLAINT)
preview: MENSTRUAL COMPLAINT · EGBO IGI IWOSAN TI ILE YORUBA 2
contentPreview: Page 4 • Menstrual Complaint • Yoruba / English
contentYoruba:
Iye aluko, ikoide, poporo ehin oka baba,iyo die, osun buke,ewe
owu,epo amuje,egbo oruwo ati egbo lali,ao gun po,obinrin na yo
ma fi mu eko gbona.
contentEnglish: Materials named in the source: aluko feather, ikoide, the back sheath of guinea-corn stalk, a little salt, osun buke, cotton leaves, epo amuje, oruwo root and lali root. Pound the materials together. The source instructs the woman to use the preparation with hot pap for delayed or absent menstruation.

sourceName: EGBO IGI IWOSAN TI ILE YORUBA 2
title: OGUN ILE TUTU
subtitle: (CHILDHOOD FEVER / BODY COLDNESS)
preview: CHILDHOOD FEVER / BODY COLDNESS · EGBO IGI IWOSAN TI ILE YORUBA 2
contentPreview: Page 5 • Childhood Fever / Body Coldness • Yoruba / English
contentYoruba:
Esan,epo ose,eru,aidan,egbo elu,egbo about,alubosa elewe,ao se
ni agbo daadaa,ao fun omo naa mu.ao si ma fi we lati orun de le.
contentEnglish: Materials named in the source include esan, epo ose, eru, aidan, elu root, abo root and leafy onion. Prepare them as a boiled herbal mixture. The source instructs giving some to the child to drink and also using it to wash the child from the neck downward.

sourceName: EGBO IGI IWOSAN TI ILE YORUBA 2
title: AGUNMU IBA TODAJU
subtitle: (FEVER / TYPHOID)
preview: FEVER / TYPHOID · EGBO IGI IWOSAN TI ILE YORUBA 2
contentPreview: Page 5 • Fever / Typhoid • Yoruba / English
contentYoruba:
Epo pandoro awon miran npe ni iyan tabi amuyan,ata dudu,egbo
oruwo,alubosa elewe,kanhun,eru,ewe ewuro ati iyo.ao gun po
daadaa,ao ma fi mu eko gbona...Odaju.....
contentEnglish: Materials named in the source: pandoro bark (also called iyan/amuyan in the source), black pepper, oruwo root, leafy onion, kanhun, eru, bitter leaf and salt. Grind everything together thoroughly. The source instructs using a small amount with hot pap and presents it as a fever preparation.

sourceName: EGBO IGI IWOSAN TI ILE YORUBA 2
title: OGUN ITO SUGAR DIABETICE
subtitle: (DIABETES)
preview: DIABETES · EGBO IGI IWOSAN TI ILE YORUBA 2
contentPreview: Page 5 • Diabetes • Yoruba / English
contentYoruba:
ao wa ako kahun bulala ,epo oronbo ,ewe koropo,obu otoyo ,ose
dudu ajo gbogbo kini yi papo pelu ose dudu ao lo ao mon fi orombo
lo laro ati lale......dan wo kio fun mi laboo abara mun pelu ase
olorun oo
contentEnglish: Materials named in the source: ako kanhun bilala, orange/lime bark, ewe koropo, obu otoyo and black soap. Combine the materials with black soap and grind them together. The source says to use it with lime/orange in the morning and at night and presents it as a traditional diabetes preparation.

sourceName: EGBO IGI IWOSAN TI ILE YORUBA 2
title: OGUN ATOSI
subtitle: (GONORRHEA / GENITAL DISCHARGE)
preview: GONORRHEA / GENITAL DISCHARGE · EGBO IGI IWOSAN TI ILE YORUBA 2
contentPreview: Page 5 • Gonorrhea / Genital Discharge • Yoruba / English
contentYoruba:
ao sun bara ni ina tio fi ro dada ao wa be epo re danu ao wa ge bara
yi wewe ao fun omire sibi kan ao wa da sugar si omire ao tun da
orombo dede omi bara yi sii ao mon mun ni sibi kan larin ijomete
meta ..........odaju gan nioo abara mun pelu ase olodu mare
contentEnglish: Roast bara on the fire until it is soft, remove the oil, and cut the bara into small pieces. The source then calls for adding a spoonful of omire, sugar and lime/orange juice to the bara liquid. It instructs taking one spoonful at intervals and presents the preparation for atosi.

sourceName: EGBO IGI IWOSAN TI ILE YORUBA 2

preview: WORMS / PARASITES · EGBO IGI IWOSAN TI ILE YORUBA 2
contentPreview: Page 5 • Worms / Parasites • Yoruba / English
contentYoruba:
Eyikeyi tabi alepe agbo gbogbo aran, Egbo sapo Egbo ifon Egbo
tude ao fi omi re ao mamu diedie laro ati lale
2.Egbo arunpale ao fi omi osanwewe re ao mamu ni gasi kokan
contentEnglish: The source gives two worm preparations. First: sapo root, ifon root and tude root are soaked in water, and a small amount is taken in the morning and at night. Second: arunpale root is soaked in lime juice, and the source instructs taking one small measure.

sourceName: EGBO IGI IWOSAN TI ILE YORUBA 2
title: OGBE NU (HULCER)
subtitle: (STOMACH ULCER)
preview: STOMACH ULCER · EGBO IGI IWOSAN TI ILE YORUBA 2
contentPreview: Page 5 • Stomach Ulcer • Yoruba / English
contentYoruba:
ogede agbagba dudu ao ge bi Eni pe afefi din dodo ao wa sa si Abe
ile tabi inu yara tobagbe dada AO LO kunna dada ao mafi wara tabi
milk lo siwaju ki ato jeun aro
contentEnglish: Cut unripe dark plantain as if preparing fried plantain, then dry it indoors or under the house until completely dry. Grind it thoroughly. The source instructs using the powder with milk before breakfast and presents it for stomach ulcer.

eso pandoro ao sa ti yio gbe dada ao wa lo kunna dada ao mafi mu
eko gbigbona sun lalale
contentEnglish: Dry pandoro fruit thoroughly, grind it into a fine powder, and use a small amount with hot pap at night. The source presents this as a traditional high-blood-pressure preparation.

sourceName: EGBO IGI IWOSAN TI ILE YORUBA 2
title: OGUN EJE RURU/H.B.P
subtitle: (HIGH BLOOD PRESSURE)
preview: HIGH BLOOD PRESSURE · EGBO IGI IWOSAN TI ILE YORUBA 2
contentPreview: Page 6 • High Blood Pressure • Yoruba / English
contentYoruba:
AO JA ESO ISIN TOBA PON DAADAA,AO JO PELU ODINDI ATARE

Fun Ogun ito sugar ti e bere fun ,,,,,,e o wa efo gbagba ti yo pon
die,omidun lafise pelu kanu bilala die tobati jina dada ,ero si inu

contentEnglish:
For high blood pressure, the source instructs taking a very ripe isin fruit, roasting it with one whole atare and using the preparation with Coca-Cola.

The same passage also gives a separate diabetes preparation: use slightly mature efo gbagba, cook it in fermented corn water with a little kanhun bilala, pour it into a keg, add six sugar cubes, and begin taking it on the second day. The source presents both preparations as effective.

sourceName: EGBO IGI IWOSAN TI ILE YORUBA 2
title: OOGUN IKO TUBERCULOSIS
subtitle: (TUBERCULOSIS / PERSISTENT COUGH)
preview: TUBERCULOSIS / PERSISTENT COUGH · EGBO IGI IWOSAN TI ILE YORUBA 2
contentPreview: Page 6 • Tuberculosis / Persistent Cough • Yoruba / English
contentYoruba:
1.Atare
2. Ata ijosi
3. Aayu
4. Egbo Igi Guava gbigbe
5. Egbo Igi Cashew gbigbe
6. Alubosa Elewe
7. Ojere epo
8. Iyo
Ao lo 1 to 6 po ni ori olo gege bi a se ma nlo ata lori olo. Ao ge eran
maalu bi oni #500 tabi iye ti owo wa ka si mesan fun okurin, meje
fun obirin, ao gbe ojere epo ka ina lori adiro sugbon a ko ni je Ki o
gba o. Ti o ba ti gbona di e, ao da elo ti a lo lori olo si pelu eran ti a ti
ge. Ao je Ki o so papo fun igba di e Ki a to fi iyo si Ki o le ni adun. Ao je
ki o jina daada. Eni to ba ni arun yi nikan ni o leto lati je obe yi. Ko si
ohunje ti ko le fi je. Arun na yio poora pelu Ase Edumare.
contentEnglish: Materials listed: atare, ata ijosi, garlic, dried guava-tree root, dried cashew-tree root, leafy onion, ojere oil and salt. Grind items 1–6 together as one would grind pepper. Cut beef into the number of pieces stated in the source, heat the ojere oil without letting it burn, add the ground materials and beef, then add salt and cook thoroughly. The source says the soup is to be eaten only by the person with the illness and presents it for tuberculosis.

sourceName: EGBO IGI IWOSAN TI ILE YORUBA 2
title: OGUN MAJELE
subtitle: (POISON / ANTIDOTE CLAIM)
preview: POISON / ANTIDOTE CLAIM · EGBO IGI IWOSAN TI ILE YORUBA 2
contentPreview: Page 7 • Poison / Antidote Claim • Yoruba / English
contentYoruba:
INJE EMO PE ITO IDIWA NSISE FUN MOJELE TI ABATIMOPE MAJELE
LAJE AOTO SINU CUP KAN AOGBEMU LESEKESE GBOGBO E LAMA
PO PADA ODAJU
contentEnglish: The source states that urine can be used against a substance believed to be poison: collect urine in a cup and drink it immediately. It presents this as an antidote claim. This is reproduced as source documentation, not as a medically verified antidote.

sourceName: EGBO IGI IWOSAN TI ILE YORUBA 2
title: OGUN ORI FIFO
subtitle: (HEADACHE)
preview: HEADACHE · EGBO IGI IWOSAN TI ILE YORUBA 2
contentPreview: Page 7 • Headache • Yoruba / English
contentYoruba:
Aoja Ewe Ata Die AO BU Iyo Die Si Ao Fowora Awafun Omi Re Si Arin
Ewe Nan Efori Nan Yiolo Lesekese
contentEnglish: Get some ata leaves and add a little salt. Rub or squeeze the leaves gently so that the liquid collects in the middle of the leaves. The source says to apply the liquid to the head and claims the headache will stop immediately.

sourceName: EGBO IGI IWOSAN TI ILE YORUBA 2
title: OGUN TI EJO BABU EYAN JE
titleOriginal: OGUN TI EJO BABU EYAN JE
subtitle: (SNAKEBITE)
preview: SNAKEBITE · EGBO IGI IWOSAN TI ILE YORUBA 2
contentPreview: Page 7 • Snakebite • Yoruba / English
contentYoruba:
AO WA Ata Ijosi Eyokan Awage Si Meji Amafipa Oju Ibiti Ejo Gbe
Buyanje Yen Yiopa Gbogbo Oro Re
contentEnglish: Take one ata ijosi, cut it into two and rub it on the place where the snake bit the person. The source claims this will neutralize the venom. This is an archival translation of the source claim, not a verified snakebite treatment.

sourceName: EGBO IGI IWOSAN TI ILE YORUBA 2
title: OGUN TI ALABOYUN KOBATETE RI OMO BI NI OJO IKUNLE
titleOriginal: OGUN TI ALABOYUN KOBATETE RI OMO BI NI OJO IKUNLE
subtitle: (LABOUR / CHILDBIRTH SUPPORT)
preview: LABOUR / CHILDBIRTH SUPPORT · EGBO IGI IWOSAN TI ILE YORUBA 2
contentPreview: Page 7 • Labour / Childbirth Support • Yoruba / English
contentYoruba:
E Wo Agbara Ewedu Ti Ao Kasi Inkan Toun Sise Fun Alaboyun Ao Ja
Ewedu Tiyiopo Die Ao Fi Omi Lasan Gbo Ao Fun Alaboyun Nan Mu
Yio Bimo Lesekese Ni Agbara Olorun.
contentEnglish: The source recommends using plenty of ewedu for a pregnant woman in labour: squeeze or prepare the ewedu with plain water and give the woman the liquid to drink. It claims this will make delivery happen quickly by God’s power.

sourceName: EGBO IGI IWOSAN TI ILE YORUBA 2
title: OGUN KOKORO INU EJE/INARUN/KURUNA
subtitle: (SKIN / BLOOD INFECTION CLAIM)
preview: SKIN / BLOOD INFECTION CLAIM · EGBO IGI IWOSAN TI ILE YORUBA 2
contentPreview: Page 7 • Skin / Blood Infection Claim • Yoruba / English
contentYoruba:
Ewe Ailu Gbigbe Yio Po Ao Ko Sinu Ike Kan Kie Da Adieyan Lelori Yiyo

The source specifically says not to add shea butter to the version intended for ifo. This is reproduced as source documentation; kerosene and gunpowder are hazardous materials.

The source says the preparation is to be taken by the patient and presents it for tuberculosis.

First version: soak epo idin in cold water as a herbal infusion and take it morning, afternoon and night.

The patient is instructed to eat a small amount daily for one week. The source presents this as an aseje for stroke.

contentYoruba:

contentEnglish:
The source presents wild honey as a material with many traditional uses and lists ten examples:

1. Eye complaint: mix honey with white onion and apply to both eyes.
2. Internal pain: mix bitter leaf with honey and take two spoonfuls after the evening meal.
3. Wound: mix bitter leaf with honey and apply to the wound.
4. Children’s teething: mix wild honey with lime juice and give one spoonful twice daily after food.
5. Tuberculosis/persistent cough: combine atare, garlic, salt and bitter kola with wild honey in a bottle; the source gives two spoonfuls three times daily.
6. Sleeplessness: take two spoonfuls of honey at night.
7. Menstrual weakness or dark/irregular flow: the source gives repeated spoonfuls of honey daily.
8. Rheumatic pain: mix bitter leaf with wild honey, apply to the painful spot and also take two spoonfuls early in the morning.
9. Boil/akandun: mix beans and kanhun with wild honey and apply to the area.
10. Ulcer: the source gives three spoonfuls of honey early in the morning about one hour before breakfast.

These are reproduced as the source’s traditional claims, not as medically verified treatments.

Eroja:
- Egusi bara to dagba

Ilana:

contentEnglish: The source claims that mature bitter melon (egusi bara) can be used for blocked fallopian tubes, fibroids, infections, ovarian cysts, cancer, arthritis and low sperm count. It gives bitter melon and fermented-corn water (omidun) as the ingredients, instructs cutting the melon into pieces and cooking it in omidun for about 30 minutes, then taking half a glass first thing in the morning and at night. The source notes that it may cause bowel movement and says mature bara is preferred. These are source claims, not medically verified uses.

It instructs drinking one glass daily and claims that this will remove accumulated salts or impurities from the kidneys. This is reproduced as the source’s claim.
